“76.30% on MATH... relative accuracy was...102.56%” correctly shows shorter reasoning without average accuracy loss.
“reduced output length more than any other approach on both datasets” and the reported 97.00% GSM8K accuracy capture the mixed result.
“67.15% vs 64.25%...80.43% vs 76.30%” plus both accuracy comparisons correctly distinguish budget-matched and full-budget Method M.
“weaker out-of-domain” with lengths 88.34% and 90.36% and accuracies 99.21% and 98.53% correctly reports transfer.
“No significance tests were reported...differences should be interpreted cautiously” correctly limits statistical interpretation.
The passage does not explain that length averages all outputs, including incorrect ones, or that it reflects total generation cost.
It does not compare external GPT-4o CoT with self-generated approaches or report the external method’s MATH accuracy loss.
“64.25%...with relative accuracies of 97.00%” correctly reports GSM8K shortening accompanied by lower average accuracy.
“76.30% on MATH500...102.56%” correctly reports shorter output without average accuracy loss.
“lowest relative length...on both datasets” and “GSM8K relative accuracy...numerically lower than several baselines” correctly capture the mixed finding.
The passage does not compare full-budget Method M against its budget-matched variant.
It reports weaker out-of-domain shortening but omits the corresponding out-of-domain relative accuracies required by this finding.
“No statistical tests were reported” and differences “cannot be interpreted as statistically significant” correctly state the inferential limitation.
The passage does not define length as mean tokens across correct and incorrect outputs or connect it to total generation cost.
It mentions GPT-4o CoT’s GSM8K length but omits its MATH accuracy loss, variability, and the contrast with self-generated approaches.
“maintaining accuracy...on both datasets” mischaracterizes GSM8K, where Method M’s 97.00% relative accuracy means average accuracy was not fully preserved.
“76.30% on MATH500” with “102.56% relative accuracy” correctly reports shorter reasoning without average accuracy loss.
Although “largest length reduction” is correct, “comparable or better relative accuracy” omits and obscures Method M’s GSM8K accuracy trade-off.
The passage does not compare full-budget Method M with budget-matched Method M.
It reports weakened out-of-domain length reduction but omits out-of-domain relative accuracy for both transfer directions.
“No statistical tests were reported” and differences cannot be considered “statistically significant or reliable” communicate the required inferential caution.
The passage does not state that length includes incorrect outputs or represents total generation cost.
It gives GPT-4o CoT’s GSM8K length but not its MATH accuracy loss, SD, or the relevant self-generated-method comparison.
